data.title: AI | Sameer Dholakia Calls Anthropic a Once-in-a-Lifetime Investment
data.description: Sameer Dholakia, a partner at Bessemer Venture Partners and an Anthropic investor, said he was “thrilled” by the Anthropic IPO and called the company a “once-in-a-lifetime” investment, according to Bloomberg. Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow said Anthropic’s focus on using computing power efficiently has led to good margins.

data.title: Greene Faults Loose BOE Policy, Not Bad Luck, for Inflation Miss
data.description: Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said the central bank can no longer blame bad luck for its struggle to return inflation to target, adding that interest rates have not done enough to contain price pressures in recent years, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Chicago Fed President Austan D. Goolsbee Says AI Buildout and Spending Could Overheat Economy
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, Chicago Fed President Austan D. Goolsbee said he was concerned that AI-related construction could overheat the economy. He said the Federal Reserve’s task of preventing that outcome was becoming more complicated.

Goolsbee said data center construction, corporate investment and consumer spending based on expectations of future wealth could contribute to overheating. He called inflation the biggest problem facing the U.S. economy and said he was concerned that tariff-driven inflation was showing greater persistence.

He added that he saw no signs of stagflation. Hiring had declined, but the labor market remained stable.

data.title: Crunch Fitness Sells $800 Million in Franchise-Linked ABS
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Crunch Fitness sold $800 million of asset-backed securities tied to franchise deals on Thursday, the latest in a recent streak of whole-business bond deals.

data.title: AI | Bipartisan House Trio Outlines AI Safety Framework Bill
data.description: A bipartisan trio of House lawmakers outlined an artificial intelligence proposal Thursday that would set minimum federal safety standards for companies, require disclosure of safety lapses and clarify liability for “foreseeable injuries” tied to the technology, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Prediction-Market ETF Approval Not Final as Parties Discuss Operations With Applicants
data.description: Bloomberg ETF analyst Eric Balchunas said on X that approval of prediction-market ETFs has not reached its final stage, with relevant parties discussing product operations with all applicants. According to Odaily, Balchunas said the process must be handled properly and called the remarks fairly optimistic for approval prospects; he said discussions appeared focused more on operating mechanisms than ethical concerns, while the outcome remains uncertain.
